description: Oscillator — square, saw, triangle and sine running at once, each with its own output, and a mixer combining all four at MIX

params.text: Sets the pitch, marked in volts, -3 to +6; 0V is C4 at 261.63Hz. V/OCT is added to it
Trims by one semitone either way
The whole range down seven octaves
Depth of the signal patched to the FM input
Pulse width of the square wave
The phase of that wave, shifting it within its own cycle before it enters the mix
How much of that wave goes into the MIX output. The OUT jack for a wave always carries it at full level, whatever this is set to
Steps the triangle wave, a sample-and-hold effect on it
FM feedback on the sine wave

inputs.text: Depth of the signal patched to the FM input
Pulse width of the square wave
The phase of that wave, shifting it within its own cycle before it enters the mix
How much of that wave goes into the MIX output. The OUT jack for a wave always carries it at full level, whatever this is set to
Steps the triangle wave, a sample-and-hold effect on it
FM feedback on the sine wave
Sets the pitch, marked in volts, -3 to +6; 0V is C4 at 261.63Hz. V/OCT is added to it

outputs.text: Square, saw, triangle and sine, each at full level whatever its MIX knob is set to
Four oscillators summed can run hot, so the menu sets whether this output is scaled to 5V, saturated, hard clipped, or left alone

menu: DC offset correction — on by default, removes the offset the square and pulse waves carry away from a 50% width; turn it off to use such an output as a CV
Mix output processing — what happens when the four waves sum past the usual range: Scaled to +/-5V, the default; Saturated or Hard clipped, both at 12V; or None, which leaves the sum alone
